svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS D11 — Chapter 11 · Ch11_ShellStructure, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 993 declarations of the 52 items on C11, each with its kind, file, line and state; 128 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 993 declarations of the 52 items on C11, each with its kind, file, line and state; 128 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted; and the items of other directories each item uses.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations · B1, the works the manuscript cites. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of C11's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card, and under it, in italics, the first sentence of its first declaration's docstring, quoted. Then the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

g.text: The character is extended trivially on the norm section. Slice integrability is written by pullback, and uniform orbit tails are assumed. The functions descending to the quotient include the character factor on the input in (11.1.1.12). The Chapter 2 approximants have inverse-character equivariance.

g.text: The polar-free theta classes are norm dense in the full global Sobolev space on the 0-line.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The cited line theorem assumes degree greater than one. Pass from a higher degree through the dense inclusion of the weighted spaces to cover every nonnegative degree in the printed statement.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The operator uses finite places as in (11.2.0.2) and the global norm (10.1.1.6), since (10.1.1.5) is S-local.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Continuity, without closed range, is stated here for every nonnegative degree and every norm twist as in the paragraph before the proposition.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: This compatibility is stated separately from closed range and holds without the lower bound on the degree.

g.text: The difference formula applies on the local-unit-invariant summand. Unramified norm-one isotypes lie in that summand by §5.3.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The reciprocal partial Euler product is the product of the unramified factors in the phase coordinates of §6.3.1.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: For PV on S use the product over S on both sides. The product over the places of S above p gives the operator for that subset. The canonical phase in [0, 2π/log q) is given by unramifiedHeckeCharacter_existsUnique_phase.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Use the strict reciprocal-weight integrability cutoff of §10.2, which excludes a logarithmically divergent endpoint of the printed floor.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The cutoff excludes the divergent endpoint.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Close the completed principal-value range in the ambient space before taking the isotype.

g.text: Sanity check for the empty set of places.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Use the conjugate isotype for the annihilator, as in the statement of jet membership. Quotienting by the closure gives the same continuous annihilator as the raw range. Index each zero of the product once with its total multiplicity. The index type permits any reindexing, including the empty family.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The paper does not state this. It shows that for a > 0 the closed range in (11.2.0.3) is the whole completion, so the successive quotients (11.3.1.3) of completed θ-images are zero: the orbital functionals χ(g)|g|^(ε-a) of Theorem 11.2.0.2 are not continuous there, and among the twists a ≥ 0 only a = 0 carries the orbital bases of §11.2.2.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The paper does not state this. The proof is a Neumann series at the test level: with A = 1 - PV_v, f = PV_v (∑_{i ≤ N} Aⁱ f) + A^(N+1) f, and the θ-class of A^(N+1) f is (|p|ᵃ R(p))ᴺ applied to that of A f, of norm O(|p|^((a+l) N) N^(s/2)).

g.text: The local absolute level is the weighted Sobolev closure of homogeneous theta from zero-moment tests whose Fourier transforms lie in the box of size Λ.

g.text: Use a positive local twist so the weighted theta functions belong to L².

g.text: Use the positive local twist of the repaired definition.

g.text: Use X = Λ as in the comparison on p. 489. Insert directly from S with the integer indicators of §7.3.2. Factoring this insertion at S′ gives the same global tests and preserves the two zero moments.

g.text: If a normalized lift preserves the printed weight's invariance under simultaneous norm dilation, every pair of equal norm with nonzero weight has relative idele integral and invertible outside a fixed finite set of places, independent of the norm and the test.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: This is a necessary restriction on a proposed replacement for (11.3.2.2).

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The paper does not state this. With such a left side, (11.3.2.1) holds at a large base exactly when its right side is zero.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The paper states (11.3.2.1) with the weight (11.3.2.2), for tests supported above norm one, without the bound by the residue size. With the printed weight it is false; with a normalized lift and a large base its left side is always zero.

'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The twisted test ψ and the uniformizers are hypotheses.

g.text: The paper does not state this. It shows that the identification on p. 496 of the shell trace with the orbital sum (11.3.2.5) fails for such a lift once the base is large.

g.text: The paper does not state this. Here the base need not contain T and need not be saturated. The packets of distinct shells are disjoint, so at every base all but finitely many shells are covered (primaryDivisorialPackets_meet_finite).

g.text: The paper does not state this. At every base, (11.3.2.1) with such a lift fails at all but finitely many shells.

g.text: Bind the displayed place in the indicated layer. Make existence of the spectral tensor used to specify the §10.4 strip kernel explicit. The counterexample uses a layer consisting of a single place.

g.text: Specialize to the first rational packet and the trivial character. Allow arbitrary kernels depending on both cutoffs, absorbing the smooth output cutoff and indentation. This gives a necessary scalar consequence of the proposed trace-norm approximation.
